title: JMeter: test plan, samplers, listeners and distributed execution

videos.script: JMeter has been testing web servers since 1998. Its window looks its age. {{window}} Under the window is a simple idea. A test is a tree. {{tree}} At the top, a group of threads. Those are the virtual users from lesson three. Under them, samplers, and each sampler sends one request. {{samplers}} Beside them, a timer that makes each user think, and an assertion that checks what came back. {{timer}} You will write that tree by hand. Fifty-eight lines of XML, two requests, one data file. {{xml}} Then you run it without the window. One command, a summary every thirty seconds, and a file with every sample in it. {{run}} You will break it on purpose, too. One bad show id, and the assertion turns it into an error. {{broken}} And when one machine is not enough, the same plan runs on several. One controller, two workers, one results file. {{workers}} Here the three machines are one VM. The mechanism is the same. {{same}}
